verifier_note: Checked all 4 recipes against midly 0.5.3's own source (src/smf.rs, error.rs, event.rs, primitive.rs, lib.rs, riff.rs), read both from the local cargo registry and freshly via WebFetch against every cited docs.rs source URL (5 unique URLs, all resolved, all midly 0.5.3, all byte-identical to the local copy). Re-ran all 9 given checks through compile_oracle.py under the jam and jam-strict oracle sets (9/9 pass originally); cross-checked every engine_note against the signed lock quoted in VERIFIER-BRIEF-W5.md, independently reconfirmed against the live docs/PHASE-0.md on GitHub. RE-ADJUDICATED export-smpte-refusal-and-error-kind-mapping-from-wasm32-strict-cdylib on coordinator-relayed evidence: reproduced myself that Timing::read (primitive.rs:495, `-(bit_range!(raw,8..16) as i8)`) negates i8::MIN and panics when the header's division high byte is exactly 0x80, under both strict and non-strict alike (Timing::read has no strict gate) - host exit 101 'attempt to negate with overflow'; the recipe's own wasm ingest() pattern does not trap on this input either, it hangs indefinitely (my wasm_call timed out at 20s, no return, no RuntimeError), worse than 'without panicking' implies. Also independently confirmed the boundary bytes: 0x81->Err(Invalid), 0xE8/E7/E3/E2->Fps24/25/29/30 - the defect is the single byte value 0x80. Separately confirmed (smf.rs, riff.rs) that strict gates neither the unknown-top-level-chunk skip (Chunk::read's `_=>()` arm) nor riff::unwrap's RMID-only/data-chunk-only RIFF handling - both unconditional in both modes - but none of this lane's other 3 recipes or their engine_notes claim otherwise, so no other verdict changed on that point. Original, still-standing finding on the other two: on the non-strict ('jam') side, 2 of 4 recipes' 'how' prose claims a specific permissive outcome (an empty resulting track after silent truncation; 0xFF masked to exactly 0x0F) that the paired check only asserts as bare res.is_ok(), never the specific value - I closed both gaps myself with independent oracle runs (tracks[0].len()==0; channel.as_int()==15) and confirmed both claims true, so those two stayed corrected rather than refuted.
